details.description: Claude Opus 5 is an Opus-tier model from Anthropic, released July 24, 2026 as the successor to Claude Opus 4.8. Anthropic describes it as a thoughtful, proactive model that comes close to the frontier intelligence of its higher Claude Fable 5 tier at about half the price, with a 1-million-token context window, vision input, adaptive thinking and stronger self-verification on agentic and coding tasks. Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22, 2026 as a newer, current Opus model, and Anthropic's own model reference now lists Opus 5 as legacy, though it remains active and available.
advantages: Scores 96.0% on SWE-bench Verified (DataCamp, reporting Anthropic's benchmark results), matching an independently reported 96% figure attributed to Anthropic's official benchmarks.
Anthropic reports its score on the ARC-AGI 3 novel-problem-solving evaluation is three times as high as the next-best model (Anthropic launch post).
Anthropic reports it surpasses Claude Fable 5's best OSWorld 2.0 computer-use result at just over a third of the cost (Anthropic launch post).
Anthropic launched it as the default model on Claude Max and the strongest option on Claude Pro (Anthropic launch post).
disadvantages: Anthropic states it remains behind Claude Mythos 5 on cybersecurity exploit-development tasks and on longer-running autonomous biology research (Anthropic launch post).
Superseded roughly two months later by Claude Opus 5.5 (September 22, 2026); Anthropic's model reference now lists it as a legacy model.
Reliable knowledge cutoff of May 2026 (Anthropic model reference).
use_cases: Agentic coding and iterative, self-verifying software engineering
Novel, multi-step reasoning and problem solving
Business process automation and workflow agents
Default assistant for Claude Max and Claude Pro users

sources.title: Claude Opus 5: Anthropic's New Flagship, Explained

notes: Catalog's deprecation_date fact (2027-01-24) does not match Anthropic's own model-deprecations table and platform.claude.com overview page, which both give a tentative retirement 'Not sooner than July 24, 2027' (exactly one year after the July 24, 2026 release -- the same pattern seen on every other Claude snapshot checked in this batch). Kept the catalog's value per instructions but flagging the roughly six-month discrepancy. Catalog's 1M max input / 128K max output tokens and image+text-in/text-out modality match platform.claude.com's specs table exactly. Anthropic's own launch post renders its benchmark table as an unreadable chart image, and its system-card PDF was too large to fetch, so exact benchmark percentages here are sourced to DataCamp's write-up of the same system card; the 96.0% SWE-bench Verified figure was independently corroborated by a separate search summary citing 'Anthropic's official benchmarks.'
